text:
Anne: Quick thread — hit a warmup stall on canary when we serve gzipped safetensors with the streaming loader. Not a full OOM, more like repeated range reads that hang.
warmup-bot: [alert] warmup-failure shard=mdl_v2_part-12 code=E_READSTALL
Jason: ugh, repro steps?
Anne: repro is small: upload gzipped shard, request model with streaming=true, warmup coordinator starts, then we see lots of `Range` retries and no progress.
Anne: log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T14:03:12Z warmup coordinator fetch range 0-65535 -> 206
2026-03-18T14:03:12Z loader verify checksum failed expected=abc123 got=000000
2026-03-18T14:03:13Z retrying range fetch backoff=50ms
```
Priya: checksum failing on first chunk sounds like decompression/codec ordering issue. Are we verifying compressed bytes or post-decompress content?
Carlos: good Q. Current loader verifies on decompressed payload (we implemented that to match safetensors checksums), but transport layer sometimes gives partial gz stream that decompresses to garbage if header split.
Jason: so two possible fixes: 1) verify compressed bytes before decompressing (if manifest stores comp-checksum) or 2) change fetch strategy to always fetch larger priming ranges to avoid header splits.
Anne: option 2 is a quick patch (bump initial range to 128k). But that increases wasted traffic for tiny shards.
Priya: long term we should make verification robust: have a per-chunk rolling checksum (or per-file compressed checksum in manifest). That lets us fail fast before decompress.
Carlos: manifest flag: `compressed_checksum` (optional). Loader behavior:
- if compressed_checksum present -> verify compressed bytes first
- else -> fall back to existing decompress+verify
Jason: also add retry policy tuned for gz streams: exponential backoff up to N=3, and a special path that, on repeated checksum mismatch, upgrades the initial fetch window instead of immediate fail.
Anne: agreed. We also need telemetry counters so we can measure how often this happens in prod: `safetensors.gz_checksum_mismatch`, `safetensors.gz_retries`, `safetensors.gz_elastic_initial_fetch`.
Priya: +1 on metrics. Also capture `shard_id` + `canary/region` tags so SRE can correlate with storage endpoints.
Jason: API boundary question — should the loader unconditionally handle gzip (transparent) or should transport layer expose raw bytes and let caller decompress?
Carlos: loader should be transparent for consistency across backends. If a storage backend sends gzipped shard, loader decompresses and exposes safetensors semantics to runtime. But transport must still expose raw checksums for verification.
Anne: implementation plan:
- short-term (canary within 1 week): bump initial range to 128k, add backoff N=3, increase logs
- medium (2–3 weeks): add `compressed_checksum` manifest field, loader verify compressed bytes first when present, emit new metrics
- long-term: RFC for chunk-level checksums and per-shard priming heuristics
Jason: tests: unit for partial gz headers, integration test using local HTTP server that serves split gz ranges, and end-to-end canary with synthetic shards.
Priya: I'll write the manifest patch and metrics PR. @Jason can you own the loader changes? @Carlos want you to handle the storage-side doc and test harness.
Jason: yep, will pick up loader PR tomorrow :+1:
Carlos: will mock S3 edge cases in storage testbed.
Anne: cool — file followup: I'll open a short RFC follow-up issue summarizing these action items and link to test checklist. Thanks all :shipit:
warmup-bot: ticket created: INF-8732 "safetensors gz checksum retry + telemetry" by Anne
